_comment: Technical Design v0.38's Setting Pack: Il Notaio's notes, then code's private and action lines, as templates. Code fills the {named} placeholders and nothing else ({currency} is the setting's plural). Copied verbatim from the engine (CC-20261111-04), so every game replays unchanged; rewording one is a content change, version-gated like a prompt. The placement lines are still stand-ins until TD drafts Il Notaio's event templates.

notes.attendance: Tonight is a smaller gathering than most: only {cast} attend. {absent} are alive, but elsewhere tonight, and can't be reached.
notes.new_group: {actor} and {other} returned to company and formed a new group.
notes.withdrawal: {actor} drew {other} aside from company — a private word, where none could hear.
notes.withdrawal_repeat: {actor} was once again seen withdrawing in private, this time with {other}.
notes._withdrawal_repeat_before_comment: TD v0.25 and earlier: the repeat note before v0.26's rewording, kept so older games replay as they ran.
notes.withdrawal_repeat_before_td26: {actor} was once again seen drawing another aside — this time {other}. Some note it is not the first private word sought this evening.

lines._payroll_comment: TD v0.50's Retitling: from TD 0.50 a payroll payment, in TD's words; each `_before_td50` key keeps the French pension's wording, so a game on an earlier TD replays as it ran. `embassy_ledger`'s {ledger} is filled from `payroll` below.
lines.pension_taken: You took a payroll payment of {amount} {currency} from the French Embassy; you are on France's payroll. Your purse: {purse} {currency}.
lines.pension_renounced: You paid back a payroll payment for {holder}: {amount} {currency} returned to the Embassy.
lines.pension_refused: Your attempt to pay back a payroll payment for {holder} failed: they have none that you can pay back.
lines.ledger_renounced: a payroll payment of {holder}'s was paid back
lines.pension_taken_before_td50: You accepted a French pension of {amount} {currency}. Your purse: {purse} {currency}.
lines.pension_renounced_before_td50: You renounced the French pension held by {holder}: {amount} {currency} returned to the Embassy.
lines.pension_refused_before_td50: Your attempt to renounce a pension for {holder} failed: no such pension that you can repay.
lines.ledger_renounced_before_td50: the pension held by {holder} was renounced

payroll._comment: TD v0.50, block 5: {payroll_status} (`no`, or `yes, 1 payment` / `yes, 2 payments`; Dominicans and the French always `no`) and the Embassy ledger's {ledger}, each guest on France's payroll with their payments ("Piero de' Medici, 1 payment"), joined by `between`, or `none`. `status_no`, `status_yes`, `one`, `many`, and `entry` are TD's words; `between` and `none` drafted by Claude Code (CC-20261114-16).

hints._comment: Il Notaio's hint to the player (TD v0.40, Il Notaio's hint): a line or two for what the moment asks, in a box under the stream, styled apart from his announcements. Templates only, no model calls. Drafted by Claude Code for Dylan's review (CC-20261112-03). `council` and `ballot` are for the full game. `errandDeadline` (TD v0.47): with plot_reward on, the last round before the errand's deadline, shown whether or not the errand is done.
hints.mingling: You're with other guests. Speak when it's your turn, or pass. Hover over anything to see what it does.
hints.answering: {name} spoke to you directly. Answer, or pass.
hints.colloquio: You're in a secret conversation with {other}. No one else can hear you, but everyone saw you leave.
hints.move: Your chance to move: stay, join another group, or start a secret conversation.
hints.seat: Your secret conversation is over. Choose where to go next.
hints.midnight: Midnight. Choose your act in secret. All acts happen at once, and no killer is named.
hints.council: Your faction is meeting alone. Only your own people can hear you.
hints.ballot: The ballot. Everyone casts one vote, and can buy more for the same candidate.
hints.refused: That didn't work. The reason is just above the message box. Type / to see what you can do now.
hints.errandDeadline: This is the last round before the last council. Finish your errand before that council to earn an extra act at midnight.
hints.dead: You've died. You can still read the web, what you heard and saw, and your notes, and you'll hear the city's announcements.

reading._comment: TD v0.44, Il Notaio's reading in the Web of Secrets: the prompt in TD names him and his trade in its own words; these replace them when the prompt is loaded. His name is in-world-names.json's narrator.
reading._guarded_comment: TD v0.51, Il Notaio's reading rebuilt around the guard (and his past-stage summaries). `line` and `lineTo` are the prompt's {lines}, one per chosen line, in TD's format; `you` names the player as an addressee, there and in his sentences; `fallback` and `fallbackTo` are G9's plain versions of a line, TD's words. `stage` opens a stage's paragraph ("In the second round of mingling:") with the stage's name as block 5 gives it, its first letter lowered. `empty`: the box's line when the player has heard and seen nothing of the selection; `emptyStage`: a past stage's, when nothing reached them. `stage`, `empty`, and `emptyStage` drafted by Claude Code (CC-20261114-19).
reading.empty: You have heard and seen nothing of them tonight.
reading.emptyStage: Nothing reached you in this stage.

room._comment: TD v0.45, Block 5's {room} (Mechanics: Everyone Sees the Room): where every other living guest is right now. Each group, then each private pair, joined by `between`, ending with `end`; a group's names joined by commas and `and`. Drafted by Claude Code (CC-20261113-04); `together` and `in private` are TD's words.
room._places_comment: TD v0.49, Named places: from TD v0.49, {room} is told place by place, each other occupied place in setting.json's order as `place` (a group, or a guest on their own) or `place_private` (a Colloquio), joined by `between`, ending with `end`; the names joined as above. `in_place` follows the conversation's kind in block 5's {conversation_label} ("a group in the loggia with …"; in-world-names.json's `conversations`). TD's words.

name._comment: Interface v0.11, Il Notaio's name glossed: `gloss` is the caption under his name at the top of the opening; `hover` shows wherever his name appears on the screen (his notes in the stream, his hint, his reading, the tour's cards), even with the hover explanations off. His glossary entry (player.json's glossary) starts with the same gloss.
name.hover: Il Notaio: Italian for “the notary”. He records the evening and belongs to no faction.

opening._comment: Interface v0.7, The Opening: the story Il Notaio writes on a full screen before the player chooses, a paragraph at a time, in this order. Fixed text, never a model call. Lore writes it and Characters canon-checks it; until then it holds only its last line, the orientation line (Interface v0.14), and the paragraphs drop in here as the list grows (#148).
opening._paragraphs_comment: Placeholder opening, Lore v0.13 (Il Notaio's Opening); the final text replaces it
paragraphs: I am the notary of this palazzo, as Florentines call a great town house, and tonight I keep its record. I write down who arrives, who speaks with whom, and who draws another aside. I belong to no faction. What follows is what every guest knew as they came through the door.

Five weeks ago, on the eighth of April, Lorenzo de' Medici died at his villa at Careggi, outside the city. For twenty-three years he ruled Florence without holding its highest office, through his bank, his friends, and his name. Three days before he died, lightning struck the lantern atop the cathedral's dome and sent marble crashing down toward the Medici houses. Many still call it a sign. His month's mind, the requiem sung a month after a death, was only days ago. Black cloth hangs at the Medici palace, and music is kept low.

In ordinary years Florence fills her offices by lot, drawing names at random from a purse of approved citizens. This spring is not ordinary. With Lorenzo gone and no one able to rule as he did, the leading houses agreed that the Gonfaloniere of Justice, the city's chief magistrate, would be chosen by vote, at a single gathering: this one. Whoever holds the office holds the city. This house belongs to no faction; its owner lent it so that no family plays host.

Lorenzo left the Medici to his eldest son, Piero, twenty-one, whom the city already calls "the Unfortunate". His younger brother Raffaello is better loved, and their cousin Clarice Orsini is the family's quickest wit. Fourteen years ago the Pazzi rose against them: Giuliano de' Medici was stabbed to death at Mass in the cathedral, and the plot's leaders hung from the windows of the Palazzo della Signoria, the city's palace of government. The Pazzi survived in name only. Tonight Francesco Pazzi, a boy when his elders fell, comes with his sister Giorgia, and no one is sure what they want.

Others will be watching the vote. At the convent of San Marco, Girolamo Savonarola, who leads its Dominican friars, preaches that Florence has grown rich and rotten, and that a scourge will come unless she repents; his followers, Friar Tommaso among them, have grown louder since. Beyond the Alps, King Charles VIII of France talks of claiming the crown of Naples, in the south of Italy, and Florence lies on his road there. France wants her friendship and can pay for it, and its Embassy has brought a royal guest: Prince Emile de Valois, the King's young cousin, sent to choose a Florentine bride.
That is all I may tell you. The rest you will learn as the guests do, by what you hear and see. Choose who you will be tonight. Speak as your character would, plainly.

tour._comment: Interface v0.8, The Tour: one card per part of the screen, in Il Notaio's voice, in the tour's order. `conversation` is step 6, the message box's card (#151 adds the warning there, Interface v0.14). `briefing` is the last: the Your briefing button, which starts the evening. Drafted by Claude Code (CC-20261114-10) for Dylan's review.

steps.sheet: This is you: your money, your payments from France, and your secret conversations. Click any line to learn more.
steps.decks: Your briefing, the rules, what the city knows, and the game's words.
steps.errand: Your errand: the one thing you came to do tonight.
steps.room: Every place in the house, and who's in it. You can see who's together, but not hear them.
steps.stageBar: The evening, stage by stage. Click an earlier stage to read it again.
steps.conversation: Type what your character says, then click Speak. Start with @ to talk to one guest, or / to act. The other guests think it's 1492, so modern talk will confuse them.
steps.right: The guest you're talking with, or the one you clicked. Only what everyone knows.
steps.web: The Web of Confidences: who's connected, what you've heard, and your notes.
